newsitem.title: UK: Ulster Unionist MPs to vote on merit - Trimble.
newsitem.headline: Ulster Unionist MPs to vote on merit - Trimble.

text.p: The leader of the nine-strong Ulster Unionist parliamentary party on Friday repeated that they would vote in the British parliament on the merits of each individual issue.
David Trimble, speaking after a meeting with opposition Labour leader Tony Blair, told BBC radio: "He knows our position in parliament -- that we do vote on the merits of particular issues."

Labour on Thursday ended the Conservatives' overall majority in parliament by winning the Barnsley East by-election. The victory means that 323 Conservative MPs now face exactly the same number of members from opposition parties.
The Ulster Unionists, who seek to retain British sovereignty over Northern Ireland, are widely seen as the most likely parliamentary prop for Major.
But Trimble said: ""There are any number of small opposition parties who have the power to help the opposition (Labour) bring down the government."

Blair, asked whether he planned to increase contacts with Trimble in the new parliamentary situation, said he would not play partisan politics with Northern Ireland. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
